findings.reason: the control as written cannot fire, so the node either records counts that do not differ (its declared control failing on a sound filter) or widens the filter until something moves and no longer measures what it names; the plan must give a control the launch-time conjunct does not already exclude, e.g. removing both conjuncts or naming a post-landing run whose session start was not connected.
findings.text: §12's negative control removes only "the connected-at-start filter" and says the 2026-11-11 local anchored runs whose tools were never offered then land in the anchored arm, but §8's membership rule — restated by §12 two sentences earlier — is connected-at-start AND launched after section 10 landed; every local anchored run whose session-start read pending launched before section 10 landed (r-20261111T130138944743 at 13:01Z on 11 November, session-start `reckon-anchored-edit: pending`; r-20261111T171926056794 at 17:19Z, probe still pending) while section 10 landed at 01:20Z on 12 November, and the only anchored runs launched after it (r-20261111T222113767813 at 22:21Z on 11 November, which is after the fast-start node landed at ~20:16Z, and r-20261111T231038123370) record `reckon-anchored-edit: connected`, so the launch-time conjunct excludes the pending runs and the connected filter excludes the connected ones, leaving no run the control can move

findings.reason: the deliverable's whole content is the per-arm comparison, and without an assignment rule the node can only produce different-work-versus-different-work, so the plan must either state the matching (run one small comparable set of sections in more than one arm, or stratify by role and node class per arm) or say that the record reports within-arm spread only and draws no cross-arm comparison.
findings.text: §12 says the coordinator produces the wave "by routing open sections to the arms" but states no assignment rule, and at about four implement runs per arm drawn from about twenty different open sections no two arms run the same work, so a per-arm table of cumulative input per run, edit failure rate and landing rate separates the sections' difficulty rather than the arms; §8's comparability sentence ("the same roles and node classes over the same window") is not restated for this wave and cannot be met by routing each section once

response_events.note: the negative control now replaces the whole membership rule with the anchored_edit launch fact alone, which admits the 2026-11-11 runs whose tools were never offered

the wave now assigns open sections to arms by a seeded random draw stratified by effort hours, records the seed and assignment, reports each arm's effort mix beside the metrics, and states that at this count the comparison is confounded by section

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — section 8's counts (30 local, 15 codex), its five arms, its policy metrics and section 10's landing all resolve in the plan text, and the two paths §12 depends on (`docs/evidence/fragments/.../` and the landed archive) exist in the repository.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §12's negative control cannot produce the difference it claims, because the membership rule it edits has a second conjunct that already excludes every run it names.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the done-when names `docs/evidence/fragments/workers-spend-fewer-tokens-per-landed-node/interim-arm-report.html`, a durable in-repo path inside a fragments directory that already holds the plan's ten other landed fragments, not a scratchpad or a node-local temporary directory.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §12 introduces no symbol, file or comment carrying a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag; the new symbols it implies (none) and the evidence filename are named by what they hold.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the interim wave has no assignment rule, so at four runs per arm over twenty different sections the per-arm table compares section mix rather than arms.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §12 delivers one artifact, an interim per-arm record, and its four prohibitions (no verdict, no flight default, no removals) keep it from carrying §8's job.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §12 is added to `plan-section-declarations` as implementable, and the missing `plan-section-depends-on` entry for s12 orders nothing that matters: an edge to s8 would invert the plan's own order (s8's verdict waits for the population s12 produces) and an edge to s10 orders nothing because s10 is done, while §12's prose names both upstreams.
